conundrums.label: Conundrums
conundrums.task_intro:
Conundrums are problems that make you think.

Watch the video carefully. There may not be one perfect answer. Decide what you think, then explain your reasoning. A strong answer tells us what you would choose, why you would choose it, and what might make someone else disagree.
conundrums.prompt_template: Watch the conundrum. What do you think should happen? Explain your choice and give at least two reasons. If there is another reasonable point of view, explain why somebody might choose it.
conundrums.top_tip_template: Make a decision first. Then give your strongest reason. Finally, test your idea: What would someone who disagrees with me say?

reflection.label: Reflection — Stoic Journal
reflection.task_intro:
Reflection is a chance to think carefully about your day.

There is no perfect answer. Choose a real moment, describe what happened, and think about what you can learn from it. Try to focus on your choices, your response, and what you might do next time.

stories.label: Silly Stories
stories.task_intro:
Silly Stories let your imagination go completely wild.

Use the prompt as your starting point, then take the story anywhere you like. Make something unexpected happen. Your job is not to make the story realistic — it is to make it entertaining while using as many of your Target Words as you naturally can.
stories.category_top_tip:
A fun story usually needs:

Somebody interesting.

Something they want.

A problem that gets in the way.

An unexpected turn.

An ending that changes something.

fortunately_unfortunately.label: Fortunately / Unfortunately
fortunately_unfortunately.task_intro:
Fortunately / Unfortunately is a story that keeps changing direction.

Begin with the prompt. Then alternate between good news and bad news:

Fortunately... something helpful happens.
Unfortunately... a new problem appears.
Fortunately... things improve again.

Keep switching until you reach an ending.
fortunately_unfortunately.category_top_tip: Every new sentence should change the situation. Do not simply say something is good or bad — make something actually happen because of it.

persuasion.label: Persuasion
persuasion.task_intro:
Persuasion means trying to convince somebody.

Choose a clear position, then give your strongest reasons. A powerful argument also thinks about what somebody on the other side might say.

You do not have to choose the answer you think an adult would prefer. You need to make the strongest case you can.
persuasion.category_top_tip:
Use this simple structure:

My position: say exactly what you think.

My reasons: give two or three strong reasons.

An example: show why one reason matters.

The other side: mention a reasonable objection.

My reply: explain why you still think your position is stronger.

prompts.title: Inside My Control
prompts.prompt_text: What was inside my control today, and what was outside my control?
prompts.top_tip: Separate the two clearly. Then spend most of your writing on what you could choose: your effort, words, attitude, preparation or response.

prompts.title: The Difficult Thing
prompts.prompt_text: What difficult thing did I deal with today?
prompts.top_tip: Tell the story of what happened, then explain what made it difficult. Finish with one thing you did well or one thing you could try next time.

prompts.title: How Big Is It Really?
prompts.prompt_text: Will this matter tomorrow, next month or next year?
prompts.top_tip: Pick one thing that felt important today. Zoom out in time. Explain how your feelings about it might change tomorrow, next month and next year.

prompts.title: An Ordinary Good Thing
prompts.prompt_text: What ordinary thing am I grateful for?
prompts.top_tip: Choose something small and specific. Instead of simply naming it, describe why it made your day better.

prompts.title: I Did It Anyway
prompts.prompt_text: When did I do something despite feeling nervous?
prompts.top_tip: Describe what you were nervous about, what you chose to do anyway, and how you felt afterwards. Courage does not mean you were never scared.

prompts.title: How I Chose to Respond
prompts.prompt_text: Something annoying happened. How did I choose to respond?
prompts.top_tip: Describe the event without spending the whole piece blaming it. Focus on the part you controlled: what you said, did, thought or decided next.

prompts.title: Advice From Tomorrow Me
prompts.prompt_text: What advice would tomorrow's version of me give me?
prompts.top_tip: Imagine tomorrow-you knows how today turned out. Write the advice as if that wiser version of you were talking directly to you.

prompts.title: What the Mistake Taught Me
prompts.prompt_text: What can I learn from something that went wrong?
prompts.top_tip: Do not just describe the mistake. Find the lesson inside it: What did it show me, and what could I do differently next time?

prompts.title: The Dragon at the Dentist
prompts.prompt_text: A dragon arrives at the dentist with a very unusual problem. Unfortunately, the dentist has never treated a dragon before. What happens?
prompts.top_tip: Give the dragon a strong personality. Make the problem get worse before somebody finds an unexpected solution.

prompts.title: No More Gravity
prompts.prompt_text: At exactly 9:17 in the morning, gravity stops working for ten minutes. Tell the story of what happens.
prompts.top_tip: Start somewhere ordinary. Then imagine the tiny details: drinks, chairs, pets, people and everything that was not tied down.

prompts.title: The Invisible Lunchbox
prompts.prompt_text: Your lunchbox has turned invisible. You can still touch it, open it and smell what is inside — but nobody can see it. Then somebody else finds it.
prompts.top_tip: Use the invisible object to create misunderstandings. Let one small problem grow into a much bigger one.

prompts.title: The Moon's Missing Treasure
prompts.prompt_text: The Moon sends you a message saying it has lost something extremely important somewhere on Earth. You have until midnight to find it.
prompts.top_tip: Decide what was lost and why it matters. Give your character clues, obstacles and a ticking clock.

prompts.title: Magic on Aisle Seven
prompts.prompt_text: A confused magician performs the wrong spell inside a supermarket. Suddenly the aisles begin behaving very strangely.
prompts.top_tip: Choose one magical rule and keep making the consequences bigger and sillier.

prompts.title: The Robot Teacher Mystery
prompts.prompt_text: You become convinced that one of your teachers is secretly a robot. What evidence do you find, and what happens when you investigate?
prompts.top_tip: Plant three clues. Make at least one clue turn out to have a completely ordinary explanation.

prompts.title: The Time Machine With One Problem
prompts.prompt_text: You discover a time machine, but it has one ridiculous flaw. Every time you use it, something unexpected happens.
prompts.top_tip: Decide the machine's strange rule first. Then let your character make the mistake of using it again.

prompts.title: A Completely Useless Superpower
prompts.prompt_text: You wake up with a superpower. Unfortunately, it seems completely useless. By the end of the day, you discover exactly why it matters.
prompts.top_tip: Make the power funny at first. Then create a problem where that exact strange ability becomes surprisingly useful.

prompts.title: You're Hired!
prompts.prompt_text: An animal arrives for a job interview and is absolutely certain it is the perfect person for the job. Tell us about the interview.
prompts.top_tip: Choose a job that is a terrible match for the animal. Let the animal explain why each apparent weakness is actually a brilliant qualification.

prompts.title: The New Door
prompts.prompt_text: A door appears in a familiar place where there definitely was not a door yesterday. Everyone tells you not to open it.
prompts.top_tip: Build curiosity before opening the door. Decide what your character expects — then surprise them.

prompts.title: The Treasure Map
prompts.prompt_text:
You find an old treasure map hidden inside a library book.

Start with: Fortunately, the map showed that the treasure was very close...
prompts.top_tip: Make each solution create the next problem.

prompts.title: The School Trip Goes Wrong
prompts.prompt_text:
Your class sets off on what should be the best school trip ever.

Start with: Fortunately, we arrived exactly on time...
prompts.top_tip: Use each Fortunately sentence to rescue the characters — then let Unfortunately spoil the rescue.

prompts.title: The Dog Who Followed Me Home
prompts.prompt_text:
A very friendly dog begins following you home.

Start with: Fortunately, the dog seemed to know exactly where it was going...
prompts.top_tip: Let the dog's behaviour solve problems as often as it causes them.

prompts.title: The Cake Disaster
prompts.prompt_text:
You are responsible for getting an enormous birthday cake safely to a party.

Start with: Fortunately, the cake looked perfect...
prompts.top_tip: Use physical problems: doors, weather, transport, animals or people in the way.

prompts.title: After Closing Time
prompts.prompt_text:
You realise everyone has gone home and you are locked inside a museum.

Start with: Fortunately, I still had my phone...
prompts.top_tip: Let the setting create your twists. Think about exhibits, alarms, guards and strange noises.

prompts.title: The Impossible Final
prompts.prompt_text:
Your team reaches the final, but everything starts going wrong.

Start with: Fortunately, we scored first...
prompts.top_tip: Keep changing who seems most likely to win until the very end.

prompts.title: Mission to Mars-ish
prompts.prompt_text:
You are on your first space mission when the computer announces that the spacecraft is going somewhere unexpected.

Start with: Fortunately, we had plenty of fuel...
prompts.top_tip: Make every new problem require a clever decision rather than pure luck.

prompts.title: The Pet With a Secret
prompts.prompt_text:
Your family brings home a new pet. On the first night, you discover it can do something impossible.

Start with: Fortunately, nobody else had noticed yet...
prompts.top_tip: Decide the pet's secret ability first and use it repeatedly in different ways.

prompts.title: Should Homework Be Banned?
prompts.prompt_text: Should children have homework after a full day at school?
prompts.top_tip: Think about learning, free time, family life and whether all homework is equally useful.

prompts.title: Who Should Choose Bedtime?
prompts.prompt_text: Should children be allowed to choose their own bedtime?
prompts.top_tip: Consider freedom, responsibility, sleep and what happens the next morning.

prompts.prompt_text: Should every home have an animal that kids help to look after?

prompts.prompt_text: Should cars be banned from busy town centres?

prompts.prompt_text: Should children have to do jobs at home to earn pocket money?

prompts.prompt_text: Should schools shorten lessons so children can have longer breaktimes?

prompts.prompt_text: Should zoos continue to exist?
prompts.top_tip: Consider conservation and education as well as animal freedom and welfare. This is a good prompt for acknowledging a strong opposing argument.

prompts.prompt_text: Should competitive video gaming count as a sport?
